title: Remove a staple without tearing the papers
instruction: Remove the staple without tearing either sheet, then slide one sheet free of the other.
context: Preparing documents for scanning requires releasing a clinched fastener while preserving thin paper around its holes.
setup: Proposed fixed setup: two white 80 gsm paper sheets, each 210 × 148 × 0.1 mm, on a 210 × 128 × 20 mm rigid document support. Sheet centres are (0.32, 0) and (0.32, 0.012) m; initial midplane heights are 768.21 and 768.33 mm; their far edges overhang by 20 and 32 mm. A steel staple has a 12.8 mm crown, 6 mm legs and 0.50 × 0.30 mm wire section, clinched through both sheets at x=0.227, y=-0.050 m. A 108 × 18 × 16 mm steel/ABS forked lever remover rests at x=0.28, y=-0.20 m. The 747.5 mm-high table and every detailed placement are in setup.json. Native settling precedes control; no sheet pins or fixed staple. Full-scene setup and screenshot are unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 when at least one whole staple leg is clear of both intact sheets. 1.0 when both legs are clear, corresponding sheet corners move at least30 mm relative to their initial12 mm stagger, and both sheets stay released for three seconds. A new tear over2 mm beyond an original hole, any new cut or puncture elsewhere, a broken staple, altered sheets or invalid evidence gives zero. Moving both sheets together does not count as separation; harmless creases do not count as tears.
run_limit: Proposed 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); no robot run yet.
reset_notes: Use fresh matched paper and one fresh staple for every trial. Record both sides before and after. Reuse the remover only while intact.
fidelity: Native steel contact produces permanent plastic bending; a no-contact control stays unchanged and halving the time step changes residual bend by 0.28%. Real 0.1 mm surface-FEM sheets have explicit puncture holes. Excess membrane strain or wire crossing intact triangles irreversibly invalidates the trial. Bending is elastic and does not retain permanent creases; a crease alone is not treated as a tear. No post-tear topology is rendered. Paper is isotropic and steel bending is currently planar. The full free-staple scene and ordinary robot extraction remain unvalidated.
scores: Not run. No demo, Dream score or media exists. This is not submission metadata.
